subject: Regional reserve scenarios for Skyline Labs — APAC/US/EU sizing and rollout
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Megan Wu <megan.wu@skylinelabs.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Mar 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Regional reserve scenarios for Skyline Labs — APAC/US/EU sizing and rollout

Megan — thanks again for the time earlier. Attached is the first-pass dedicated capacity proposal and three sizing scenarios we discussed. High level summary below, plus questions where we need your signal to finalize pricing/lead times. Attachment: 20260315-skyline-dedicated-sizing.xlsx and skyline-commitment-term-sheet-v1.pdf

Quick context: Skyline's product mix suggests heavy inference in APAC (real-time chat), moderate steady throughput in US (background embeddings + batch jobs), and EU growth for inference-by-request. We tied capacity to the three deal milestones in the term sheet (pilot, M1, enterprise).

Sizing scenarios (per region) — conservative | baseline | aggressive (GPUs and type):
- APAC: conservative 8x H100-80GB | baseline 16x H100-80GB | aggressive 28x H100-80GB
  - Rationale: real-time latency targets, sequence length 512 median, expected 25 qps sustained during peak micro-bursts. H100 recommended for NVL/sequence concurrency and multitenant isolation.
- US: conservative 6x A100-80GB | baseline 12x A100-80GB | aggressive 20x A100-80GB
  - Rationale: heavier batch/embedding workloads; cost-sensitive so A100 baseline with quantization profiles.
- EU: conservative 4x A100-80GB | baseline 8x A100-80GB | aggressive 12x A100-80GB
  - Rationale: initial footprint then scale based on year-over-year growth and GDPR review window.

Assumptions used in the workbook: average tokens per request 150, token throughput per GPU measured on representative model (redwood-gpt-xl) at 220 tok/s for A100 and 380 tok/s for H100 at target quantization; expected utilization target 60-75% to maintain latency SLOs. We included a cost-per-hour delta for burst buffer capacity and regional cloud premiums.

Questions for Skyline to finalize:
1) Which scenario aligns to your Q2/Q3 commit (Conservative/Baseline/Aggressive)?
2) APAC latency SLO — is 200ms p95 acceptable or do we need 120ms p95?
3) Can procurement sign the attached term sheet or do you need a separate PO process?

Operational notes and recommended rollout:
- Pilot (2-4 weeks): start with 25% of baseline capacity in a single AZ in APAC; use canary traffic from 2 geos.
- M1 (60–90 days): scale to baseline across APAC+US; enable KV caching and batching profiles we recommend.
- Enterprise: aggressive option only if traffic growth exceeds 30% MoM for two consecutive months.

Please review the workbook. If you’re comfortable we’ll convert baseline into a reserved pool quote and produce a DocuSign term. HubSpot deal link and Drive file are in the attachments. Lauren and Neha — flagged for sizing validation and lead-time confirmation (15–20 day procurement lead typical for H100 in APAC).

Best,

Subject: Re: Regional reserve scenarios for Skyline Labs — APAC/US/EU sizing and rollout

Megan — thanks for the quick read and the clarifying asks. Answers inline below and next steps. Quoting your email for clarity: 

> - APAC: baseline latency target is 150ms p95... will H100 baseline meet that at 60–75%?

Short answer: yes. We validated the baseline H100 curve against your median sequence length and observed ~140ms p95 under our 60% utilization target with prefix caching enabled. Neha ran the microbench and I’ve attached the kernel-level notes to the Drive link. If you want a hard SLA at 120ms p95 we recommend adding a 20% headroom (i.e., bump baseline APAC to 20x H100) or adding a local read-through cache layer to shave cold-starts.

> - Burst: do you offer a short-term burst pool (1–2 days) over reserved? If so, price uplift?

Yes — we offer a burst buffer via Dedicated Burst (pre-warmed ephemeral instances). Pricing: +45% over reserved hourly for H100 and +30% for A100. Minimum 8-hour block and 24-hour billing granularity. We can pre-approve a single burst event per quarter under the term sheet at a discounted uplift of +30% for H100.

> - Compliance: legal wants location guarantees for EU data and persisted logs

We can commit to EU-only data residency for EU-scoped customers (logs and persisted KV) and will include the clause in v2 of the term sheet. There is an operational note: for cross-region failover we’ll maintain metadata necessary for routing but will not persist customer content outside EU without explicit consent. I’ll have legal draft the text and return by Wed.

Operational timeline if you sign baseline APAC and conservative EU today:
- Week 0–2: PO + execution of term sheet; procurement to supply billing contact and PO number.
- Week 2–4: procurement/ordering and capacity reservation (H100 lead times 15–20 days as noted).
- Week 4–6: pilot activation in APAC with canary traffic and dashboards.

Next steps I propose: you and procurement confirm baseline APAC, attach PO; we then generate a DocuSign for signature and flip the dedicated reservation. Lauren — can you confirm we’ve accounted for the KV cache config and the 2-AZ failover plan (I flagged this in the workbook). Neha — confirm lead times for H100 in SG and any vendor exceptions.

If it helps we can do a short technical readout with your SREs this week to validate latency numbers on your payloads.

Thanks — Ben
